beats: Hook: every new attention idea used to need its own hand-tuned GPU kernel; now it is a three-line Python function. [line_flex_smith_pegboard, line_flex_card_machine]
FlashAttention made attention fast by working tile by tile in fast on-chip memory, but only for the variants it hard-coded. [line_glue_tiles, line_press, line_gpu]
The zoo: causal, sliding window, document masks, relative position, ALiBi, soft-capping: each needed its own kernel. [line_flex_smith_pegboard, line_three_readers]

score_mod: one small function changes each score as it is computed (from b, h, q_idx, kv_idx): a relative bias without storing a giant N x N table. [line_flex_table_vs_card, line_flex_listen_distance]

Soft-capping: score -> cap * tanh(score / cap) keeps scores from growing too large (a soft ceiling); ALiBi: farther tokens count a little less. [line_flex_softcap_cushion, line_temp_knob, line_flex_listen_distance]

mask_mod returns yes or no for each pair: causal (only look back), sliding window (only the last few), documents (only your own document). [line_flex_stencil_roller, line_flex_slide_window, line_flex_doc_tables, line_scroll_ends]
The block mask skips tiles that are fully masked: causal skips about half (check), sliding window and documents far more. [line_flex_garden_skip, line_glue_tiles]
How: torch.compile turns the functions into a Triton attention template, forward and backward. [line_flex_card_machine, line_token_mill]

Inference: one new token against a long KV cache (up to 128k): split the cache across the GPU like Flash Decoding and apply score_mod; paged KV via block-mask conversion at under 5% overhead, 76x larger batch (check; PagedAttention itself is L13-03: one line). [line_flex_long_shelf, line_card_catalog, line_clerk_ladder]
Results: on par with hand-written decoding kernels; LLaMA3.1-8B 1.22-2.04x over SDPA (check). Takeaway: write the rule; the compiler writes the kernel. [line_flex_card_machine, line_whisper_line]
